meta.description: FLUX.1-dev LoRA for a 16GB laptop GPU. This is the highest-risk preset in the folder for this card: flux_lora_24gb, which this is derived from, is named for a 24GB card and FLUX.1-dev is a 12B-parameter model - fp8 quantization alone does not bring it under 16GB with comfortable margin. Recipe values are UNCHANGED from flux_lora_24gb (Ostris' canonical train_lora_flux_24gb.yaml: rank 16/16, sigmoid timesteps, adamw8bit, LR 1e-4, EMA 0.99); only memory/IO settings differ. Deltas: (1) low_vram true - the 24gb preset leaves this unset, which is the single most important gap for a 16GB card; it parks idle components on CPU, which is cheap in memory terms with a large system-RAM pool. (2) Training resolution [512, 768] instead of [512, 768, 1024] - the 1024 bucket is the most likely OOM trigger here. Re-add 1024 if a run proves it fits; this is a memory tradeoff with a real quality cost, not a free win. (3) cache_latents true alongside cache_latents_to_disk, so latents are served from RAM instead of re-read and deep-copied from disk every step (native Windows runs the dataloader at num_workers 0, so disk reads are serialized with GPU compute). (4) Preview sampling at 768 instead of 1024. (5) ui_db_poll_seconds 2 throttles the UI's per-step sqlite polling; the only cost is up to 2s of latency on the stop/save-now buttons. NOT verified on 16GB hardware - no FLUX run has been made on this machine. If it OOMs anyway, the next levers are layer_offloading true with layer_offloading_transformer_percent around 0.35 (see krea2_lora_16gb for that pattern), then dropping to resolution [512]. Note that enabling layer_offloading silently rewrites qtype qfloat8 to float8 (toolkit/config_modules.py:721). Speed (2026-08-29): latents are served from RAM after the first pass (cache_latents + cache_latents_to_disk — disk-only caching re-read every latent every step), loss_sync_every 4, ui_db_poll_seconds 2. Training math unchanged.
